objective: Prevent Android Community Wall feed fallback and cooldown recovery requests from starting while their ad row is off-screen, without blocking first-view or non-Wall sponsored surfaces.
productionBaselineEvidence: Current Main already tracks current visible Community feed ad-row IDs in useBuklodCommunityAdViewability and uses a sticky activation state to avoid repeated requests. The Android NativeAd renderer did not consume the current visibility hook for its delayed BannerAd fallback or recovery, so a NativeAd failure/no-fill arriving after a row was scrolled away could still start an off-screen fallback request. The current production renderer also has a separate viewport gate for first-view placements.
chosenApproach: Wire useBuklodCommunityInlineVisibility(slotId) into the Android NativeAd renderer and gate only the sequential BannerAd fallback and cooldown recovery for ordinary Wall feed rows. Explicitly bypass the feed-row registry for firstView and non-Wall surfaces, which continue using their existing viewport/route/consent gates.
selectionRationale: Reuse the already-maintained current-visible-row registry rather than adding another scroll listener or changing feed activation semantics. This prevents delayed off-screen fallback/retry requests while preserving sticky activation, shared cooldown, and first-view behavior.
preserveBehaviors: NativeAd remains the primary request and BannerAd remains sequential fallback.
Only ordinary Android Wall feed rows use the live list-visibility gate.
Public Wall first-view, Home, Profile, Connect and Cluster dashboard ads bypass the feed registry and retain their existing viewport gate.
UMP consent, SDK readiness, network, foreground, route safety, remote placement kill switches, shared reservations and cooldowns remain authoritative.
No new ad requests, IDs, SDK packages, database changes, or native runtime changes are introduced.
acceptanceChecks: Android Wall feed fallback waits until its slot ID is in the current visible-row registry.
Cooldown recovery does not restart a failed Wall feed ad while the row is off-screen.
First-view ads and non-Wall sponsored surfaces remain independent of the feed-row registry.
The production OTA AdMob regression harness executes the new visibility regression.
Engineering Accountability, focused Node tests, TypeScript/Performance R1 QA and Main integration QA pass.
No production OTA is triggered by this PR.
alternativeApproaches: Gate all NativeAd and BannerAd surfaces on the feed-row registry; rejected because first-view, Home, Profile, Connect and Cluster surfaces do not publish feed-row IDs.
Add another independent scroll observer to every Android ad card; rejected because the existing list viewability registry already provides the authoritative current-visible state.
Gate only the first BannerAd fallback but allow cooldown recovery off-screen; rejected because a failed slot could still restart a new NativeAd request after being scrolled away.
